answer: An agent economy resists sybils by requiring each identity to earn a reputation stake that grows only when peers independently co-sign its work. A new agent sits at the inlet of a narrow funnel: trusted agents must confirm its first outputs, and each confirmation goes on-ledger. Clones get nothing free, so every fake key repeats the full costly sequence. When many new keys share one funding vertex or vote in lockstep, the graph exposes them and peers withhold attestation. Like an ember that must warm its tinder first, influence is earned hop by hop, making sockpuppets dearer than honest work.
